newsitem.title: ROMANIA: IMF Board to discuss restoring loans for Romania.
newsitem.headline: IMF Board to discuss restoring loans for Romania.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund Board will discuss on April 22, earlier than expected, a letter of intent from Romania's government to resume credits of some $400 million, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said.
"The date for the discussion was brought nearer and the IMF Board will approach the issue of restoring credits to Romania on April 22," Isarescu told reporters on Monday.
The Fund and Romanian officials had previously said the IMF Board would analyse renewed loans for Romania on April 23.
The IMF halted loans to Romania last year complaining that the leftist government -- which lost elections last November -- was delaying reforms and had restricted currency markets.
Earlier this month, Poul Thomsen, the IMF chief negotiator for Romania, said the country's chances to secure credits were "very good" and that the reform programme was on schedule.
Isarescu said fresh IMF financing would be an "extremely favourable signal" for the country's credibility.
"The IMF's approval will give a green light to foreign investors."
Romania's new centrist coalition government, headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, pledeged to step up reforms.
So far, Ciorbea's cabinet has implemented liberalisation of staple and fuel prices, allowed the exchange rate to find a realistic level and pledged to shut down inefficient industries.
The parliament also rushed to pass a 1997 tough budget and a bank privatisation law in a bid to meet reform promises.
